questions.q: Under UAP Document 202, what is the specific service phase where the architect provides professional advice in the selection of the contractor?
questions.n: This phase involves the architect assisting the owner in evaluating bids and selecting the most qualified contractor for the project.

questions.q: What is the primary zoning classification of the project site in Antipolo?
o: R-1 (Residential 1), which typically denotes Low Density Residential.
C-1 (Commercial 1), which typically denotes Neighborhood Commercial.
R-3 (Residential 3), which typically denotes High Density Residential.
R-2 (Residential 2), which typically denotes Medium Density Residential.
questions.n: R-2 classification specifically allows for medium-density housing such as duplexes or townhouses commonly found in subdivisions.

questions.q: What type of architectural service is requested that includes concept design and contract documents?
questions.n: Regular Design Services encompass the sequential phases from schematic design to construction documents and bidding.

questions.q: Who is the primary target market for this 3rd subdivision development?
questions.n: OFWs are a major demographic for suburban housing developments in areas like Antipolo due to their investment capacity.

questions.q: What is the specific building type commissioned for this project?
questions.n: The single-attached typology shares a firewall, optimizing lot usage for a 2-bedroom family setup.

questions.q: In the context of "fair return of investment," what should the architect prioritize in the material selection?
o: The most expensive luxury finishes to attract high-end buyers.
Cost-efficiency and durability to balance developer profit with buyer satisfaction.
The cheapest available materials to maximize developer profit.
Imported materials regardless of lead time.
questions.n: Material selection must provide value-for-money to ensure the developer profiting while the buyer receives a long-lasting home.

questions.q: Since the LA (Licensed Architect) provides contract documents, which document specifies the quality of materials and workmanship?
questions.n: Specifications are the written instructions that detail the standards of quality, installation methods, and material properties.

questions.q: What is the minimum number of years an architect is civilly liable for the structural collapse of this house?
o: 15 years per the Civil Code of the Philippines.
questions.n: Article 1723 of the Civil Code mandates a 15-year liability period for architects and engineers in case of structural failure.

questions.q: How many family members are explicitly mentioned as the target occupants for the design?
questions.n: The project brief specifically identifies a starting family consisting of three members.

questions.q: What is the first phase of the architect's regular design services for this project?
questions.n: The schematic phase involves translating the client's requirements into initial spatial concepts and site studies.

questions.q: In a single attached house, what is the term for the wall that sits on the property line and has no openings?
questions.n: A firewall is a non-combustible wall designed to prevent the spread of fire between buildings on adjacent lots.

questions.q: What is the minimum setback requirement for the front of a residential R-2 property?
questions.n: For R-2 zoning in the National Building Code, 3.00 meters is the standard front setback for residential structures.

questions.q: For a 2-storey residence, what is the minimum required thickness of a load-bearing CHB exterior wall?
questions.n: Exterior load-bearing walls are required to be at least 150mm thick to ensure structural stability and resistance to weather.

questions.q: What is the minimum ceiling height for the first floor of a naturally ventilated room?
questions.n: The Building Code mandates a minimum of 2.70 meters for the first floor to allow for better air circulation in naturally ventilated buildings.

questions.q: What is the minimum area required for a master bedroom in a residential house?
questions.n: According to the Building Code, the minimum area for any room used for human habitation is 6.00 sqm.

questions.q: What is the minimum clear width for the main entrance door of the house?
questions.n: 0.80m is the mandated minimum clear width for the primary entrance to ensure accessibility and furniture movement.

questions.q: What is the minimum horizontal dimension for a kitchen in this unit?
questions.n: The Building Code specifies 1.50m as the minimum least dimension for a kitchen to ensure functional workspace.

questions.q: To ensure natural light and ventilation, what is the minimum window opening area relative to the floor area of a room?
questions.n: The National Building Code requires at least 10% of the floor area to be provided as window openings for light and air.

questions.q: What is the minimum required width for a private stair in a residential building?
questions.n: Private stairs in a residential unit are permitted to have a minimum width of 0.75m.

questions.q: What is the maximum height of a stair riser for a residential unit?
questions.n: The Building Code limits residential risers to 200mm to ensure they are not too steep for safe everyday use.

questions.q: What type of footing is most appropriate for a single attached house on stable soil?
questions.n: Isolated footings for columns and wall footings for the perimeter walls are the most efficient and common for light residential loads.

questions.q: What is the standard concrete mix ratio (Class A) for the columns and beams of this house?
questions.n: Class A concrete (1 part cement, 2 parts sand, 4 parts gravel) is the standard structural mix for beams, columns, and slabs.

questions.q: What material should be used for the kitchen counter to ensure it is sturdy and long-term?
questions.n: These materials offer high resistance to heat, scratching, and moisture, making them ideal for heavy kitchen use.

questions.q: What type of rebar is commonly used for the main longitudinal reinforcement of the columns?
questions.n: Deformed bars provide mechanical bonding with concrete, and 12-16mm sizes are standard for small residential columns.

questions.q: What board material is best used for eaves and ceiling in bathrooms to resist moisture?
questions.n: Fiber cement is water-resistant and does not rot or swell, making it the superior choice for wet areas and exterior eaves.

questions.q: What is the purpose of placing "Stirrups" in the beams of this 2-storey house?
o: To prevent the concrete from drying too fast.
To resist shear and diagonal tension.
To provide tensile strength to the bottom of the beam.
questions.n: Stirrups are essential to prevent the concrete from cracking diagonally under the shear forces found near supports.

questions.q: Which brand of power tools is commonly recommended for the contractor to use on site for precision cutting?
questions.n: These are industry-standard professional brands known for durability and accuracy on construction sites.

questions.q: What type of roofing material provides a balance of aesthetic appeal for OFWs and durability?
o: Pre-painted Rib-type Long Span G.I. Sheets.
questions.n: Rib-type long span sheets offer a modern look, come in various colors, and have fewer joints to prevent leaks.

questions.q: What should be used to protect the wood trusses (if any) from termite infestation?
questions.n: A combination of ground-level barrier (soil poisoning) and direct wood treatment (preservatives) provides comprehensive protection.

questions.q: What material is used for the "pantile" or roof cover to ensure leak-proofing?
questions.n: Sealants and metal flashings are critical at transitions and joints to ensure water cannot penetrate the roof envelope.

questions.q: Where should the Septic Tank be located in a single attached house layout?
o: Directly under the living room floor.
At the highest point of the backyard.
Usually under the driveway or front yard, accessible for cleaning.
questions.n: Placement in the front allows for easy access by 'siphoning' trucks without entering the private house areas.

questions.q: What is the minimum slope for the sanitary sewer pipes leading to the septic tank?
questions.n: A 2% slope (approx. 20mm drop per meter) ensures enough velocity for solids to be carried by the water without settling.

questions.q: How many switches are needed to control a hallway light from both the first and second floors?
questions.n: A 3-way switch setup allows a single light to be toggled from two different locations, like the top and bottom of a stair.

questions.q: What is the standard height for an electrical convenience outlet from the finished floor line?
questions.n: 300mm is the standard mounting height for wall outlets to keep them accessible while hiding cords near the floor.

questions.q: What device is used to prevent sewer gases from entering the 2nd-floor bathroom?
questions.n: The P-trap holds a water seal that acts as a physical barrier against foul-smelling and toxic sewer gases.

questions.q: What is the standard voltage for the residential electrical system in Antipolo?
questions.n: The standard nominal voltage for residential power in the Philippines is 230 volts at 60Hz.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a "Vent Stack" in the plumbing system?
o: To store extra water for emergencies.
To drain the rainwater from the roof.
To provide air circulation and prevent siphonage of trap seals.
To increase the water pressure in the shower.
questions.n: Vents equalize pressure in the pipes, ensuring that falling waste doesn't 'suck' the water out of the P-traps.

questions.q: What is the function of a Circuit Breaker in the house's electrical panel?
o: To store electricity for use during a brownout.
To protect the circuit from overcurrent or short circuits.
To convert AC power to DC power.
questions.n: Circuit breakers 'trip' and cut off power when they detect a dangerous surge, preventing fires and equipment damage.

questions.q: Which brand of plumbing pipes is locally known for high-quality PPR or PVC?
questions.n: These are leading local manufacturers recognized for producing pipes that meet Philippine and international standards.

questions.q: What is the standard height for a kitchen sink counter from the floor?
questions.n: This range is ergonomically optimal for most adults to work at the sink without excessive back strain.

questions.q: Given the project is in Antipolo (often hilly), what must be considered during the site layout?
o: Installing a swimming pool on the highest point.
Making sure the roof is flat for sunbathing.
The number of coconut trees to be planted.
Grading, drainage, and potential retaining walls if the lot is sloping.
questions.n: Sloping sites require careful management of soil levels and water runoff to prevent erosion and foundation issues.

questions.q: To make the house "attractive" for OFWs, what exterior finish can be used on the facade?
o: Textured paint, Wood Plastic Composite (WPC) accents, or stone cladding.
Corrugated iron sheets as wall cladding.
questions.n: These finishes provide a modern, high-end look that appeals to buyers looking for aesthetic value in their investment.

questions.q: For a starting family of 3, where is the most functional placement for the common T&B?
o: Under the stairs, even if the ceiling is only 1 meter high.
In a separate building at the back of the lot.
Accessible from the common areas on the ground floor and near bedrooms on the 2nd floor.
questions.n: Placing the bathroom where it serves both guests (ground floor) and residents (bedrooms) maximizes utility.

questions.q: What type of window is best for maximizing the breeze in the higher elevation of Antipolo?
questions.n: Casement windows open 100% and can 'scoop' the breeze into the house more effectively than sliding types.

questions.q: If the developer wants a "sturdy" feel for the stairs, what material should be specified?
o: Reinforced Concrete stairs with wooden or tile finish.
questions.n: Concrete provides a solid, noiseless, and vibration-free feel that conveys 'sturdiness' to homeowners.

questions.q: What is the "Contractor's Profit" usually estimated at in a residential project?
o: 0%, since they only work for the experience.
questions.n: This is a standard industry range that allows the contractor to sustain their business while remaining competitive.

questions.q: How is "Single Attached" different from "Single Detached"?
o: Single attached shares one fire wall with a neighbor; single detached has yards on all sides.
Single attached has two storeys; single detached has only one.
Single detached is only for rich people.
questions.n: The defining characteristic of 'attached' is the shared wall on one property line to maximize lot area.

questions.q: What is the standard size of a bedroom door for the 2nd-floor rooms?
questions.n: This width is standard for interior bedroom doors, balancing space-saving with functional access.

questions.q: What document must the architect sign and seal to apply for the building permit?
o: A personal letter to the Mayor.
questions.n: The Building Official requires signed and sealed plans to ensure they were prepared by a licensed professional.

questions.q: What is the primary advantage of using "Ready-Mix Concrete" for the 2nd-floor slab pouring?
o: It is cheaper to buy in small amounts.
You don't need any labor to spread it.
Consistent strength and faster construction time.
questions.n: Ready-mix is batched in a controlled plant, ensuring accurate ratios and allowing for large volumes to be poured quickly.
